name: Johnson & Johnson
description: Johnson & Johnson is a healthcare holding company with two reported segments. Innovative Medicine (64 percent of FY2025 sales) sells patent-protected prescription drugs in oncology, immunology, neuroscience, pulmonary hypertension and infectious diseases, mostly through wholesalers and pharmacies. MedTech (36 percent) sells surgical tools, orthopaedic implants, heart-rhythm and heart-pump devices and eye-care products to hospitals and eye-care professionals. It no longer has a consumer-health segment (the 10-K reports only the two). Nearly all profit comes from drugs: Innovative Medicine earned 84 percent of segment pre-tax profit, and results lean on a few blockbusters (DARZALEX, STELARA, TREMFYA) whose patent expiries drive the numbers. In October 2025 it announced it will separate its Orthopaedics business.

employees.note: Approximately 138,200 employees worldwide per the 10-K business section.

businessLines.name: Innovative Medicine
businessLines.how: Sells patented prescription drugs to wholesalers, pharmacies and hospitals, repeat purchases by patients on chronic or cyclical therapy; revenue rides on a handful of blockbusters until patents expire and generics or biosimilars take the sales (STELARA fell 41.3 percent in 2025). Three wholesalers were 21.8, 15.5 and 11.1 percent of total company gross revenues in 2025.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (52 weeks ended 2025-12-28), segment income before tax

businessLines.name: MedTech
businessLines.how: Sells surgical instruments, orthopaedic implants, cardiovascular devices (electrophysiology catheters, Abiomed heart pumps, Shockwave) and contact lenses to hospitals and eye-care professionals; device sales tied to procedure volume plus recurring disposables.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (52 weeks ended 2025-12-28), segment income before tax

brands.name: Intra-Cellular Therapies (CAPLYTA, $700M in 2025 Neuroscience sales)
brands.note: Acquired 2025-04-02; Intra-Cellular and Halda Therapeutics together cost $17.5B net of cash acquired in 2025

whatsNext.when: target about April to October 2027 (computed from the announcement)
whatsNext.text: Separation of the Orthopaedics business, targeted within 18 to 24 months of the October 2025 announcement; separation costs of $0.3B in Q2 2026 and $0.4B in the first six months of 2026
